# Three-minute project updates

Synthetic source for testing Cadence, not an institutional policy.

A useful project update helps the audience understand the current state and make a decision. State the purpose, report the most relevant evidence of progress, name the obstacle or uncertainty, and make a specific request or next step. Choose details for the audience; do not read a complete activity log.

An example update: "The welcome guide is drafted. Three new staff members tried it; two could not find the help contact. We need the contact owner confirmed today so we can publish the guide Friday."

Learners can practise by preparing an update about a low-stakes office project, delivering it to a partner, and receiving feedback about clarity and whether the request was actionable. Partners should describe what they heard before suggesting a revision. A second attempt lets the speaker apply feedback.

One earlier pilot used an 80% written final exam. That was the pilot's grading arrangement, not a general recommendation or institutional requirement. The supplied subject material does not establish that a written exam measures oral briefing performance.
